Following an earlier report from Counterpoint Research showing Apple's iPhone shipments reached their strongest-ever performance in the second quarter, Omdia has now released its own data, also pointing to this record result. Details below.

Omdia warns that larger declines are still to come

Earlier, we reported on a report from Counterpoint Research showing preliminary data for global smartphone shipments in the second quarter of 2026.

Counterpoint's report noted that Samsung led the market with a 24% shipment share, up from 20% a year earlier. Apple followed closely at 20%, up from 17% last year; Xiaomi fell from 14% to 12%, OPPO from 12% to 11%, and vivo from 9% to 8%.

Now, Omdia's preliminary report (as cited by MacMagazine) also points to the same overall trend, although its estimates differ slightly.

Omdia placed Samsung at 22%, up from 20% in Q2 2025; Apple followed closely at 20%, up from 16% last year. Xiaomi fell from 15% to 11%, OPPO from 12% to 10%, and vivo from 9% to 8%.

Below is Omdia's commentary on Apple's performance this quarter:

Unsurprisingly, Omdia said the ongoing memory chip crisis caused overall shipments to fall 4% year-over-year, making Q2 2026 the weakest quarter for the market since Q2 2023.
